source.title: GeNAS: Neural Architecture Search with Better Generalization
source.authors: Joonhyun Jeong; J. Yu; Geondo Park; Dongyoon Han; Y. Yoo

record.file_problem: none; full paper text including appendices is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a flatness-based measurement ranks architectures by generalization performance, using NAS-Bench-201 ground-truth test accuracy and transfer evaluations. Its method is an architecture-search proxy rather than the direct weight perturbation/generalization-gap comparisons in V7.
record.gate_note: The paper measures loss flatness and reports how its architecture rankings relate to benchmark test accuracy, plus accuracy of selected architectures on ImageNet and other tasks. Table 1's angle-flatness correlation is a metric comparison; rows below focus on reported measures/results relevant to generalization. Its introduction's cited findings about batch size, flat minima and regularization are prior work, not this paper's results. Out-of-distribution and downstream-task results are outside the claim versions.
record.test_reason: GeNAS uses the flatness–generalization hypothesis to build an architecture-search tool. Its results measure architecture-score correlations with test accuracy and selected architectures' performance. They do not test V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance against training–test gaps among networks with similarly low training loss. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that their flatness-based proxy can identify generalizable architectures and improve conventional NAS scores, with strong transfer, distribution-shift, and downstream-task performance. Their implemented default proxy combines flatness with loss depth; they explicitly report that flatness alone can select suboptimal architectures.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a Gaussian-noise flatness score to rank subnet architectures in a one-shot NAS framework, with Kendall’s Tau against benchmark test-accuracy ranks and transfer accuracy as outcomes; does not measure magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or train-test gap among similarly low-training-loss networks.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with perturbation range, whether all parameters or only search-cell weights are perturbed, perturbation direction, the α balance between flatness and minima depth, and γ when flatness is combined with angle or accuracy scores.

fits_no_version.finding: The combined flatness-and-depth score ranks benchmark test accuracy with Tau 0.6047 on CIFAR-10 and 0.5800 on ImageNet16-120 at the default range. Rankings depend on perturbation range, α, position, and direction; flatness alone gives Tau 0.1777 on CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A validation-loss score combining sensitivity to additive Gaussian weight noise with loss depth can predict architecture test-accuracy rankings in a weight-sharing NAS setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding the flatness-and-depth score to angle-based search raises selected-architecture ImageNet top-1 accuracy from 75.00% to 75.72%; adding it to accuracy-based search gives comparable or slightly lower results at small weights and reaches 75.85% versus 75.37% at the largest tested weight.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Combining a flatness-and-depth proxy with conventional NAS scores can improve selected architectures' transfer accuracy, depending on the score and combination weight.

fits_no_version.finding: Combining angle and validation accuracy produces mixed selected-architecture ImageNet accuracy, ranging from 74.26% to 75.32% against the 75.00% angle-only baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The performance of combined angle-and-accuracy architecture search depends on the combination weight.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.1 and Figure 2 describe the lowest-test-accuracy architecture group as having the flattest validation-loss minima but higher loss values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unscaled validation-loss flatness alone can favor poorly performing architectures when loss depth is uncontrolled.

record.peer_reviewed: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI 2023)
record.problems: The study evaluates architecture-ranking correlation and downstream test accuracy, not the training-test gap directly. It does not test magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance as specified in V7. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the relevant tables. Table 5/Table 6 are benchmark aggregate rank-correlation results, not per-trained-network gaps.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for other standalone architecture-search metrics and the SOTA method comparisons in Tables 2–4 were excluded because they report the selected architecture's performance or compare the study's search method, rather than measure flatness or a gap between training and test error. Distribution-shift and downstream-task results were also excluded because those outcomes are explicitly outside the claim's scope.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy; random-label held-out chance performance.
Test-error behavior when widening beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, underfitting, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.

The entire specified relation: magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance versus training–test error gaps among networks with similarly low training loss, including comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both V7 verdicts. Differences in search-proxy performance do not establish support, scope limits, or challenges for V7. The perturbations are additive Gaussian noise without weight-magnitude scaling, and the measured loss is validation loss. No training–test gap comparison or matching on low training loss is reported. E6's asserted limitation is not supported by its attached quotation.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out generalization.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Large versus small batch training under epoch budgets.

The study compares flatness-based architecture ranking with benchmark test accuracy and examines flatness-measure settings, but does not measure within-family training-test gaps among similarly low-training-loss networks, nor magnitude-scaled weight perturbations or the specified norm- and margin-based comparisons.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: NAS-Bench-201 ranking on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet16-120 using the default perturbation range and α = 1
reader_labels.reason: Flatness-and-depth search has Kendall’s Tau 0.6047 on both the default range and α = 1, with the paper reporting improved discrimination of generalizable architectures (R4, R8, R13).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Perturbation range, perturbation position and direction, and combined search-metric settings
reader_labels.reason: Rank correlation falls with too-small or too-wide ranges, search-cell-only or Hessian perturbations, while flatness combinations show mixed outcomes across γ values and compared metrics (R2-R3, R5-R7, R9-R12, R14-R17, R19-R27).
